back: A rule giving exactly one output $f(x)$ for each allowed input $x$.
Domain: the allowed inputs. Range (image): the outputs actually produced.
$f(x)=mx+b$: slope $m$ (change in output per unit input), intercept $b=f(0)$. Graph is a straight line.
Roots of $ax^2+bx+c=0$: $x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$. The discriminant $b^2-4ac$ says: >0 two roots, =0 one, <0 none (real).
$a_nx^n+\dots+a_1x+a_0$; degree $n$ is the largest power. At most $n$ real roots.
$f(x-h)$ moves the graph $h$ right; $f(x)+k$ moves it $k$ up.
$c\,f(x)$ stretches vertically by $c$; $f(x/c)$ stretches horizontally by $c$.
$-f(x)$ flips over the $x$-axis; $f(-x)$ flips over the $y$-axis.
$(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$: apply $g$ first, then $f$. Order matters.
$f^{-1}$ undoes $f$: $f^{-1}(f(x))=x$. Exists when each output comes from exactly one input; its graph mirrors $f$'s over $y=x$.
A model is a function with adjustable constants; a loss is a function of those constants; a layer is a composition of simple functions.
